---
title: "R Data Visualization"
output: html_notebook
---

Prerequisites for the visualization

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

We will use this data set for visualization

```{r}
data("starwars")
print(starwars)
drop_na(starwars)
```

To plot a scatter plot between Height and Mass

```{r}
ggplot(data=starwars,aes(x=starwars$height,y=starwars$mass))+
  geom_point(color="blue",size=2)+
  geom_smooth(method=lm)+
  labs(title="Mass vs Height in the Starwars Character",x="Height",y="Mass")
  theme_bw()
```

To get a glimpse of the dataset

```{r}
glimpse(starwars)
```

To create a new data set and convert height as double

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  mutate(height = as.double(height))
```

Now lets select height and mass while also removing the missing values

```{r}
starwars_2 <- starwars %>% 
  select(height,mass) %>% 
  drop_na %>% 
  print()

```

Now with the data lets try to find the correlation between height and weight

```{r}
cor(starwars_2$height,starwars_2$mass)
```

This shows there is a relative positive relationship between the height and mass

Now lets make a linear model between the two variables

```{r}
mod <- lm(data=starwars_2,mass~height)

```

Now lets generate a summary of our model

```{r}
summary(mod)
```

From the Multiple R squared it yells us that 1.7% of mass can be explained by using the height.This shows us that this is a weak model

Now lets predict the following observations

```{r}
pred <- data.frame(c(50,60,70))
print(pred)

```
